Why two quotes for the same Evergreen Park house come out different

Masonry walls change the exterior job completely. On 11.2 percent prewar stock and a 1955 median, there is very little painted wall outside: the work is the porch, the cornice, the soffit, the fascia, the garage surround and the sash. All of it is detail, most of it is off a ladder, and none of it is quotable from a photograph. 6,109 households own in Evergreen Park and 1,219 rent, which produces two different phone calls. One wants the house to look right for ten years. The other wants a unit clean and let by the first of the month. Both are real work and neither should be quoted like the other.

What an estimate here has to account for

  • Distance, stated. Evergreen Park is 5.6 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Evergreen Park is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 93.2 percent of housing in Evergreen Park was built before 1980, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6.1 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.
  • Whole elevations. 85.8 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is postwar brick: bungalow, Cape Cod and the first generation of ranch. Little of the outside takes paint at all, so an Evergreen Park exterior is soffit, fascia, overhangs, doors and the garage. Inside it is small rooms with a great deal of casing in them.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1955 median build year, and the split between 85.8 percent detached houses, 1.4 percent attached homes and 12.9 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Evergreen Park is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

What the age of Evergreen Park houses means for lead paint

Most of Evergreen Park went up in the 1950s, which is well before 1978, and paint made before then can contain lead. That does not stop a house being painted. It changes how the room gets sealed off, how the dust is kept out of the rest of the house, and what the place looks like when the day ends.

What it changes is the front and the back of an Evergreen Park job, not the middle: plastic and sealed openings before, a specific cleanup standard after. It starts at roughly six square feet of disturbed paint per room inside, twenty square feet outside, and always on window replacement.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Evergreen Park.

Of the 7,707 housing units counted in Evergreen Park, 93.2 percent went up before 1980. There is no pre-1978 bucket, so 1980 is the nearest line the Census draws for Evergreen Park. The federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule applies to work that disturbs paint in housing built before 1978, and in Illinois the EPA administers it directly rather than through a state program.

None of that is a reason to leave an Evergreen Park house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Evergreen Park has 7,707 housing units and a median build year of 1955. 93.2 percent of them were built before 1980, 87.7 percent before 1970 and 11.2 percent before 1940. Those three numbers together describe the walls, the trim and the windows better than a photograph does.

Evergreen Park is 83.4 percent owner occupied, 6,109 households against 1,219 renting. 12.9 percent of units are in buildings of two or more, 1.4 percent are attached, and the remaining 85.8 percent are detached houses averaging 6.1 rooms. The Census puts the median home value at $255,700.

Evergreen Park is in the top four of the 54 suburbs and towns covered here for the largest share built before 1970 (87.7 percent), the oldest housing stock overall (93.2 percent built before 1980) and the oldest housing by median build year (1955).

Three figures put Evergreen Park a long way from the average of the 76 places on this site: townhomes and rowhouses at 1.4 percent against a 7.5 percent average, housing in buildings of two or more at 12.9 percent against a 29 percent average and housing built before 1970 at 87.7 percent against a 56.9 percent average.

Questions

Asked about Evergreen Park

What changes the price most on a house here?

The state of the trim and the ceilings. Wall area is predictable, and with 6.1 median rooms and a 1955 median build year in Evergreen Park the woodwork is where the hours actually go. Ask for it as its own line and the differences between two quotes stop being mysterious.

Does the lead-safe rule apply to my house in Evergreen Park?

Probably, and the honest answer is that your build year decides it rather than the town. 93.2 percent of housing units in Evergreen Park went up before 1980, so most addresses here land on the pre-1978 side of the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. It applies to work that disturbs paint, at roughly six square feet per room inside or twenty square feet outside, and to any window replacement. Check the year on your own address and ask whoever quotes you how they handle it.

Most of Evergreen Park is owner occupied. Does that change anything?

It changes what the work usually is. At 83.4 percent owner occupied, with 6,109 owner households, there is very little turnover painting here and a lot of repeat maintenance: exteriors on a cycle, one room at a time inside, trim and doors when they finally go. A maintained house and a neglected one are different jobs and should be different numbers, in both directions.

My house in Evergreen Park is plaster, not drywall. Is that a problem?

It is not a problem, it is a different repair. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the fix has to address the movement rather than the line. With a 1955 median build year most of Evergreen Park is plaster over lath on at least some walls and ceilings. Say so when you call, because it changes the time estimate and it is better said before the quote than after.
